title: Manifest
description: A Project's identity, and the commands the platform runs inside its images, in one committed file. The two halves have two owners: the identity - slug, appName, appHost, profile, contractVersion - is written by `project new` and never edited, because everything outside the repository was named after it; the commands, inside the Add-ons that need them, belong to the Project and change when its stack does. Read by the Project's workflows, by the contract check, and by anyone who opens it (ADR-0010).

$schema.description: Optional. Points an editor at this file; the checker reads the schema from its own checkout, not from the network.

slug.description: The Project's name everywhere a machine reads it: the Compose project name, the Traefik router and service names, the directory on the host, the image repository. Lower case, digits and hyphens. A leading digit is allowed, because a real Project has one and Compose accepts it.

appName.description: The Project's name where a person reads it.

appHost.description: The public hostname. Read at image-build time as well as at deploy time - the frontend bundle is compiled against it - so changing it means republishing, not redeploying.

profile.description: The Template this Project was copied from, which is what the Template decided on its behalf beyond the contract: how images are built, how tests run, and in some Profiles a language. `base-dockerfile` names none. A closed list on purpose: the contract names no language, and a Profile is the one place a language may appear, so adding one is a contract version bump rather than a free-text field.

provider.description: Which engine backs this Project's database. The platform runs exactly one, and the `addon-provider` rule is where that list lives - so a provider the platform does not run is reported in the same verdict as every other rule rather than as a schema error nobody can read beside the rest. The key is here so that the Manifest stops asserting, in its own shape, that there could never be a second one; adding a second value is a change to ADR-0005 rather than a change to the shape of this file.

service.description: The Service of docker-compose.prod.yml whose image runs the command. The `addon-commands` rule checks that the Stack has it.

command.description: Run as `sh -c '<command>'` in place of the image's entrypoint, in a one-off container of that Service's image, with DATABASE_URL in its environment. CONTRACT.md says why a shell.

migrate.description: How this Project's schema is brought forward. The deploy runs it in the new release's image, before the new images serve; a failure leaves the previous Release serving. Forward only: there is no down-migration on this platform.

service.description: The Service of docker-compose.prod.yml whose image runs the command. The `addon-commands` rule checks that the Stack has it.

command.description: Run as `sh -c '<command>'` in place of the image's entrypoint, in a one-off container of that Service's image, with DATABASE_URL in its environment. CONTRACT.md says why a shell.

seed.description: How an empty database is filled with synthetic data, for a Preview. Never a copy of production - that is what keeps a Preview and its testers outside production's Trust Domain. The Profile runs it on every CI run against a throwaway database, because a declared command nobody has run is a Manifest field that is false.

database.description: An optional dependency on the shared Postgres (ADR-0005). Declaring it commits this Project to what docs/addons/database.md in doden-contract describes, and a copy of that document travels with the Add-on. It carries the two commands the platform runs against the database, so neither can exist without it.

addons.description: The optional dependencies on Shared Platform Services this Project declares (ADR-0013). Keys are the Add-ons; each value carries that Add-on's configuration, and an Add-on with nothing to configure takes an empty object. A Project with no Add-ons writes {}. Traefik and the web network are not in here: every Project depends on them and none declares them, which is what *optional* means. A capability a Project implements for itself - a login, a scraper, a third-party integration - is not an Add-on, however much code it takes and however many Projects write it.

contractVersion.description: The major version of the Platform Contract this Project is held to, matching the tag its workflow pins and the version its CONTRACT.md carries.
